fixes.explanation: A king? Friend, that's a fun guess, but you went shopping in a different verse! The first thing the LORD names is “…rains in their season…” (Leviticus 26:4) After that come the land's produce and the trees' fruit. No throne in sight, just weather and fruit trees.

Wet grain? Nobody in this verse is fussing about soggy grain, friend! The LORD says, “You will still be eating the old supply of grain when you need to clear it out to make room for the new.” (Leviticus 26:10) The trouble here is having so much grain that the old has to be cleared out for the new. I'd take that trouble any day.

Small? Baker, this verse is the opposite of small! The LORD says, “You will still be eating the old supply of grain when you need to clear it out to make room for the new.” (Leviticus 26:10) You're still chewing on last harvest and the next one is knocking. I've had batches where I wished for that kind of problem.

Zion is a fine mountain, friend, but it's not the one on this card. The closing verse says the LORD established these laws “…through Moses on Mount Sinai.” (Leviticus 26:46) Moses is the one the LORD sent to bring His people out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10). Nice swing, though. Wrong mountain, right spirit!

Carmel! Baker, you picked a mountain, so you're in the right neighborhood. But the verse ends with the laws the LORD established “…through Moses on Mount Sinai.” (Leviticus 26:46) Carmel never comes up in this passage. The sermon wraps up right at Sinai.
